slug: 2025-12-15 Strengthening Civil Registration and Ending Statelessness in South Sudan

facts.fact: Hold the Child's project snapshot states that South Sudan has adopted a Costed Plan for the Civil Registration and Vital Statistics System and recently approved Civil Registry Rules and Procedures, with implementation constrained by limited infrastructure and institutional weakness; the adoption is undated, so the published date is used.
facts.system: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) System

facts.fact: The birth-registration pilot is resourced by Vital Strategies, and the project supporting its roll-out at Juba Teaching Hospital is costed at USD 85,000 with USD 48,000 still sought from donors, per Hold the Child's snapshot published 15 December 2025; no domestic budget is mentioned.

The birth registration work is carried out with the Ministry of Interior's Department of Civil Registry, Nationality, Passport and Immigration (DCRNPI), implemented by the NGO Hold the Child with a technical working group of UN agencies and Vital Strategies, per the snapshot published 15 December 2025.

Hold the Child's snapshot states that the country is yet to issue birth certificates and national identity cards at scale, birth registration having only been piloted within existing constraints; undated, so the published date is used.

systems.owner: DCRNPI, with Hold the Child; resourced by Vital Strategies
systems.tiers: pilot in Juba, at Juba Teaching Hospital; light equipment to be provided for its roll-out there

systems.system: Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (CRVS) System
systems.tiers: a costed plan adopted; not stated
piloted; about 10% of the population hold a Nationality Certificate

note: The document does not say whether the Juba pilot records births digitally or on paper, so no fact is recorded for how the record is made or for offices.
